Zabdi
zăb´dī
n. (the grandfather of Achan, of the tribe of Judah)
Hebrew Zabdi, meaning my gift or endowment. He is named only in the account of Achan's sin, where the lot narrows household by household until it reaches him and then his grandson.

Biblical Definition

The name appears in the sentence that explains a military defeat: “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel” (Joshua 7:1). One man had taken spoil from Jericho, and the text says the children of Israel committed the trespass. The search that follows narrows by stages: “And he brought the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zarhites: and he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man; and Zabdi was taken” (Joshua 7:17). Then the household: “And he brought his household man by man; and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken” (Joshua 7:18). And the whole house is gathered for judgment: “And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had” (Joshua 7:24). Zabdi is in the story because the lot fell on him first, and his grandson was standing in his tent.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Zabdi; the name belongs to the grandfather of Achan, of the family of the Zarhites in Judah.

ZABDI, n. The grandfather of Achan, of the family of Zerah in the tribe of Judah.

ACCURSED, a. Doomed to destruction or misery; separated from the use of man and devoted to destruction.

LOT, n. That which in human speech is called chance; the determination of Providence by casting or drawing.

TRESPASS, n. Any voluntary transgression of the moral law; any violation of a known rule of duty.

SOLIDARITY, n. The state of being jointly and severally answerable; community of responsibility.

Key Scripture

Joshua 7:1 — "But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel."

Joshua 7:17 — "And he brought the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zarhites: and he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man; and Zabdi was taken:"

Joshua 7:18 — "And he brought his household man by man; and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken."

Joshua 7:24 — "And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor."

Modern Corruption

The account is rejected as primitive collective punishment, which passes over what the chapter actually teaches about a covenant community and the way sin is uncovered within it.

expand to see more

The modern objection is that a whole family suffered for one man's theft, and it is not a frivolous objection. Scripture's answer is not that individual responsibility is unreal — Ezekiel insists at length that the soul that sinneth, it shall die, and Deuteronomy forbids putting fathers to death for children. What Joshua 7 asserts is that Israel was one body under covenant, that a devoted thing hidden in one tent defiled the camp, and that the narrative itself records the sons and daughters being brought out with the silver and the garment, which suggests a household that knew what was buried under the floor.

The chapter's enduring lesson is the slowness of the exposure. The lot came tribe by tribe, then family by family, then man by man, and Zabdi was taken before Achan was. Achan stood through every narrowing round with the chance to speak and did not, until the lot reached him, and then he confessed fully and accurately. Sin hidden in the camp is not merely a private matter with private consequences; it cost thirty-six men at Ai before anyone knew why. The New Testament reasons the same way about a congregation — a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump — and gives the church a procedure precisely so the narrowing need not be by lot.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Zabdi (H2067), my gift; cherem (H2764), a devoted or accursed thing; goral (H1486), a lot; maal (H4603), to act treacherously.

expand to see more

Hebrew Zabdi (H2067) — my gift; grandfather of Achan, of the Zarhites.

Hebrew cherem (H2764) — a devoted thing, under the ban; the accursed thing taken.

Hebrew maal (H4603) — to act unfaithfully, commit a trespass; Joshua 7:1.

Hebrew goral (H1486) — a lot; the means by which the household was narrowed.

Hebrew Zarchi (H2227) — a Zarhite, of the family of Zerah in Judah.

Usage

"“Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi” — the man behind the defeat."

"“And Zabdi was taken” — the lot reaching the household."

"“The children of Israel committed a trespass” — how one man's theft is described."
